title: Explicit twist frame on a product standard chart
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}A_j$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], with twists and canonical homogeneous sections as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Let $d,n\geq1$, $\alpha,\beta\geq0$, $\alpha=\beta+d$, and $a\in A_\alpha$, $b\in A_\beta$. Put $h=ab$, $V=D_+(h)$, and $R=A_h$, the localization at the powers of $h$, with $A_j=0$ for $j<0$ and degree parts $R_j=\{z/h^t:z\in A_{j+t(\alpha+\beta)},\ t\geq0\}$. Both $a$ and $b$ are units in $R$. The element $e=(a/b)^n=a^{2n}/h^n\in R_{nd}$ has inverse $e^{-1}=(b/a)^n=b^{2n}/h^n\in R_{-nd}$. Multiplication by $e$ gives an $R_0$-linear isomorphism $R_0\simeq R_{nd}$ with inverse $t\mapsto e^{-1}t$. These maps commute with all standard-open localization restrictions inside $V$ and induce an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal O_V\simeq\mathcal O_P(nd)|_V$ sending $1$ to $e$. For every homogeneous $f\in A_{nd}$, the canonical section on $V$ has expression $f/1=c e$, with $c=b^nf/a^n\in R_0=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and the same expression holds on every subopen of $V$.

source.place: Tag 01MU (lemma-where-invertible), first paragraph of proof: generator (a/b)^n; Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), proof: expression f/1=(b^n f/a^n)(a/b)^n.

proof.text: Put $k=\alpha+\beta=2\beta+d>0$. In $R=A_h$ the inverse of $a/1$ is $b/h$, and the inverse of $b/1$ is $a/h$: their products are $ab/h=1$. Hence $(a/b)^n=a^{2n}/h^n$ and $(b/a)^n=b^{2n}/h^n$. Their product is $a^{2n}b^{2n}/h^{2n}=1$. The numerator degrees are $2n\alpha=nk+nd$ and $2n\beta=nk-nd$, respectively, so these elements belong to $R_{nd}$ and $R_{-nd}$ as asserted. No cancellation in $A$, and no nonzero hypothesis on $a$ or $b$, is used.

source.place: Tag 01MU (lemma-where-invertible), first paragraph of proof: generator (a/b)^n; Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), proof: expression f/1=(b^n f/a^n)(a/b)^n.

proof.text: For $r=z/h^t\in R_0$ one has $er=a^{2n}z/h^{n+t}\in R_{nd}$, because its numerator has degree $2n\alpha+tk=(n+t)k+nd$. For $v=z/h^t\in R_{nd}$ one has $e^{-1}v=b^{2n}z/h^{n+t}\in R_0$, because its numerator has degree $2n\beta+nd+tk=(n+t)k$. Both operations are well-defined multiplication by fixed elements of the commutative ring $R$ and are $R_0$-linear. Their two composites are the identity since $ee^{-1}=1$. This proves the claimed module isomorphism and its precise inverse.

source.place: Tag 01MU (lemma-where-invertible), first paragraph of proof: generator (a/b)^n; Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), proof: expression f/1=(b^n f/a^n)(a/b)^n.

proof.text: For a positive-degree homogeneous $g$ with $D_+(g)\subseteq V$, let $\lambda_g:A_h\to A_g$ be the localization restriction from [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2). The section modules on this chart are $(A_g)_0$ and $(A_g)_{nd}$. The images $e_g=\lambda_g(e)$ and $\bar e_g=\lambda_g(e^{-1})$ have degrees $nd$ and $-nd$ and satisfy $e_g\bar e_g=1$. Multiplication by them therefore gives inverse $(A_g)_0$-linear maps between these two modules, by the degree calculation of Step 2. For a further standard-open inclusion with localization map $\lambda$, the identities $\lambda(e_g r)=\lambda(e_g)\lambda(r)$ and $\lambda(\bar e_g v)=\lambda(\bar e_g)\lambda(v)$ show compatibility in both directions. The restrictions of the section $e$ are exactly the $e_g$.

source.place: Tag 01MU (lemma-where-invertible), first paragraph of proof: generator (a/b)^n; Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), proof: expression f/1=(b^n f/a^n)(a/b)^n.

proof.text: The positive-degree standard opens $D_+(g)$ contained in $V$ form a basis of $V$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion] (0) states that the standard opens $D_+(g)$, $g$ homogeneous of positive degree, form a basis of the topology of $P$, and that $D_+(g)\cap D_+(h)=D_+(gh)$. Hence for $x\in V$ and an open neighbourhood $N\subseteq V$ of $x$ there is such a $g$ with $x\in D_+(g)\subseteq N$, and every chart $D_+(g)$ meets $V$ in the standard open $D_+(gh)\subseteq V$, of positive degree $\deg g+k$. By (1) of the same node, for $D_+(g)\subseteq V$ the element $h$ is a unit of $A_g$, so the localization map $\lambda_g:A_h\to A_g$ of Step 3 exists.

source.place: Section 01M3 (label section-proj), paragraph before Lemma 01M4 (standard opens form a basis, $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$); Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (a) on the topological space $V$, with values in abelian groups, to the underlying additive sheaves of $\mathcal O_V$ and $\mathcal O_P(nd)|_V$. Their basis sections and restrictions are those of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2). Steps 3--4 supply inverse compatible families on this basis, hence two sheaf morphisms. Their composites are identities because this is true on each basis open, and uniqueness in (a) detects equality there. They are $\mathcal O_V$-linear: for sections $u,s$ on an arbitrary open, restrict to each basis member; the equality $\Phi(us)=u\Phi(s)$ holds there by Step 3, and the sheaf separation axiom gives equality on that open. The same argument applies to the inverse. This gives the stated module-sheaf isomorphism; on $V=D_+(h)$ its map is $r\mapsto re$, so it sends $1$ to $e$.

source.place: Tag 009O (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence) and Tag 009U (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules), applied to the compatible fraction maps in Constructions Tag 01MU

proof.text: For homogeneous $f\in A_{nd}$, [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (3) identifies its canonical section on $V$ with $f/1\in R_{nd}$. Its coefficient under the inverse frame is $c=e^{-1}(f/1)=b^{2n}f/h^n=b^nf/a^n$. The middle expression exhibits it in $R_0$: its numerator has degree $2n\beta+nd=nk$. Multiplying by $e$ gives $ce=(b^{2n}f/h^n)(a^{2n}/h^n)=f/1$. By (2) of the same definition, $R_0=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Restricting the equality of these sheaf sections gives the same coefficient expression on every subopen of $V$, with $c$ and $e$ restricted there; no assertion that arbitrary subopens are affine is needed.
